newsitem.title: USA: Dallas-Fort Worth airport mulls $1.7 bln expansion.
newsitem.headline: Dallas-Fort Worth airport mulls $1.7 bln expansion.

text.p: The Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, the country's second-busiest, is mulling a $1.7 billion expansion over the next five years, an airport spokesman said on Tuesday.

Plans also are on the drawing board for up to $2 billion in improvements to the airport over the next 20 years to handle an expected doubling to 100 million passengers and 1.5 million takeoffs and landings a year, he said.
"We need to continue to improve the airport to meet the future demand both from passenger traffic as well as airline takeoffs and landings," airport spokesman Joe Dealy said.

The airport plans to spend about $90 million in the next two years to expand hub operations for AMR Corp's American Airlines. Plans call for refurbishing four existing gates and adding five new gates, along with construction of infrastructure like parking and baggage handling, he said.

The project would be financed with joint revenue bonds from the airport and the sister cities of Dallas and Fort Worth, along with a $3 per ticket passenger surcharge and contribution from the airline, Dealy said.
Built on an 18,000 acre tract, the airport and its four horseshoe-shaped terminals with 118 gates occupy about one-third of the available land.

The $1.7 billion project, which would have to gain backing from Fort Worth-based American Airlines, calls for an additional 30 to 50 gates initially and eventual construction that could double the number of existing gates, Dealy said.

Plans for the $2 billion expansion include an overhaul of terminals throughout the airport, construction of a new rail system to replace an existing tram and rerouting roads leading into the massive airport.
A decision on the first phase of the expansion is due by year-end and construction could begin as early as next year, Dealy said.
